visual_roadmap.layout_logic: Heavily relies on Protocol Time-Sequence Diagrams (Figures 4-7) to demystify complex handshakes. Uses a 'Research Gap' figure (Fig 1) immediately in the intro to visually anchor the paper's value proposition.

writing_style_secrets.phrasing_patterns: Consistently uses a 'Summary and Lessons Learned' subsection at the end of every major technical section (Sections III, IV, V). This provides periodic 'rest stops' for the reader to synthesize complex technical info.
writing_style_secrets.technical_depth_management: Manages complexity by strictly adhering to the defined taxonomy (Architecture -> Method -> Variant). Never discusses a protocol without referencing which architecture it applies to.

top_3_tips: Implement 'Micro-Conclusions': Don't wait for the end. Add a 'Lessons Learned' subsection after every major technical chapter to summarize insights immediately.
Visual Gap Proof: In your related works table, add a specific column that checks for your paper's main topic (e.g., 'MAP-Co Study'). Seeing a column full of 'No' or 'Brief' is powerful justification.
Taxonomy is King: If your topic is complex, define a strict classification tree (e.g., Centralized vs Distributed) early and force every subsequent subsection to fit into that tree.
mistakes_to_avoid: Describing complex handshake protocols with text only. You MUST use time-sequence diagrams (like Fig 4-7).
Mixing generic wireless terms with standard-specific ones. Stick to the emerging standard's specific terminology (e.g., NDPA, BRP, Trigger Frame in 802.11be).
